Did the pen camera capture the horror writer in the act of committing a physical, literal murder of another person inside his home?

The narrator planted a hidden camera pen on a favorite horror writer as a birthday gift, intending to spy on him in his own home. After the party, the narrator reviewed the footage and was horrified because the camera captured the writer committing a real, literal murder inside his home—revealing that the writer was not merely an author of horror fiction but an actual killer. The narrator's horror stems from discovering the writer's genuine crime through the surveillance he himself secretly arranged.
Did the pen camera capture the horror writer murdering a person who was the narrator's own creation, alter ego, or otherwise a part of the narrator rather than a separate individual?
Did the narrator recognize the murder victim in the pen camera's footage as himself or as someone he knows?
Did the narrator realize that the horror writer had used the pen camera's recorded murder to frame the narrator for a crime (e.g., planted the pen or footage where police would find it)?

The narrator secretly gave his favorite horror writer a pen containing a hidden camera, intending to spy on the writer inside his own home. After returning home, the narrator reviewed the footage and was horrified: the pen camera had recorded the writer committing a real, literal murder of another person in his home. This revealed the writer was an actual killer, not merely an author of horror fiction. The narrator's horror came from discovering this genuine crime through the surveillance he had secretly arranged.
